study_population.definition: YouTube channels monetizing through Patreon before the widely publicized 2015 hack-related extortion versus later Patreon-adopting YouTubers not on Patreon during comparison

identification.treatment: pre-attack Patreon creators subject to disruption
identification.comparison: later adopters who had no Patreon account during evaluated period

heterogeneity.population: creators in top decile of average pre-period viewership

interpretation_gates: 2015 Patreon subscriber loss is a historically dated shock, not a forecast of present-day YouTube memberships or security conditions.
33.59% is the treated sample's revenue change; do not call it the DiD causal estimate or use it as a universal Patreon churn rate.
7.7% is a conservative regression-based relative decline in publication frequency conditional on parallel trends, selection, model and matching assumptions.
Affiliate and sponsorship increase describe observable incidence and link mentions, not confirmed advertiser-paid gross or creator net income.
Historical 10-minute video-duration indicator proxies ad-roll eligibility; it cannot establish actual ad placement, impression count or creator advertising revenue.
Absence of a statistically significant viewership change is not evidence of zero economic audience cost.
Early- versus later-Patreon-adopter groups are not a random sample of all YouTube entrants and may differ in reach, content, locale and production costs.
recommended_followup: If creator-authorized data become available, measure gross sponsorship, affiliate receipts, native ad payouts, recurrent fan receipts and net labor/cash costs as independent revenue components, with dated counterfactual comparison.
